claims.text: Severe plastic deformation followed by short-duration, low-temperature annealing can simultaneously enhance yield strength and tensile ductility in a room-temperature-brittle MPEA.
The proposed processing route introduces a high density of coherent nanoscale precipitates and a dislocation substructure that promotes strain hardening without premature fracture.
The initial MPEA has high yield strength, negligible tensile ductility, and brittle fracture behavior at room temperature.
The initial coarse-grained or as-cast microstructure has limited intrinsic strain-hardening capacity.
High-pressure torsion or equal-channel angular pressing will induce ultrafine grain refinement and a high dislocation density.
Annealing below the solvus but above the recovery temperature will trigger nanoscale precipitation and dislocation rearrangement.
The applicable processing window is SPD at room temperature to 200°C and strain rate above 1 s^-1, followed by annealing at 300–500°C for 10 minutes to 2 hours.
The treatment will produce a dual-phase microstructure with ultrafine grains smaller than 1 µm.
The ultrafine grains will contain a high density of coherent nanoscale L12 or B2 ordered precipitates.
The resulting dislocation-cell structure will impede dislocation motion while facilitating cross-slip and strain hardening.
SPD grain refinement will increase yield strength through Hall–Petch strengthening.
Short annealing will nucleate coherent precipitates without coarsening them.
The coherent precipitates will pin dislocations through Orowan strengthening.
The SPD-generated dislocation substructure will enable dynamic strain aging or geometrically necessary dislocation accumulation.
Enhanced strain hardening will delay necking and fracture and thereby overcome the strength–ductility trade-off.
The treatment will increase yield strength by more than 20% relative to the initial state.
The treatment will increase uniform elongation by more than 10 percentage points and increase total tensile ductility.
The treated alloy will exhibit non-brittle fracture with visible plastic deformation before failure.
Standard solution annealing followed by slow cooling or standard aging typically produces either coarse, low-strength grains or coarse embrittling precipitates without substantial ductility recovery.
The proposed response is limited to MPEAs capable of forming coherent nanoscale precipitates and may fail when precipitates are inherently brittle or grain-boundary cohesion is too low.

contradictions.description: The stated conventional baseline is solution annealing followed by slow cooling or standard aging, whereas the purported standard-aging control is SPD followed by long annealing. Because that control retains the SPD intervention, it is not the same standard thermal-treatment baseline described elsewhere.

The precipitates are described as coherent but are assigned Orowan strengthening without explaining whether they are non-shearable. Coherent nanoscale precipitates are often treated through cutting or coherency/order strengthening, so the stated mediator and bypass mechanism are not fully coherent.
